articles.originalTitle: Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography Exhibition Guide - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern Explores the Pictorialist Photography Movement in a Major Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern presents a comprehensive exhibition exploring pictorialism, the first international art photography movement, bringing together over 200 rare vintage prints.
articles.content: Tate Modern hosts Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography from October 14, 2026, to February 21, 2027, focusing on the pictorialist movement. The exhibition examines the dawn of pictorialism, which asserted that photography is a genuine art form as expressive as painting or drawing. Featuring over 200 rare vintage photographic prints from around the world, the display highlights darkroom experiments, platinum prints, bromoil processes, and various analogue techniques. Beginning in the 1880s, pictorialism led photographers to draw inspiration from painting regarding composition, texture, and aesthetic impact. Visitors can explore a working darkroom within the exhibition, where on select days they can learn to create photographic prints using vintage and environmentally friendly techniques. Admission is free for members at Tate Modern.

articles.originalTitle: snøhetta unveils completed shanghai grand opera house with spiraling public rooftop - Designboom
articles.title: Shanghai Grand Opera House Opens on the Banks of Huangpu River
articles.excerpt: Designed by Snøhetta, the Shanghai Grand Opera House spans 146,786 square meters and features a spiraling public rooftop alongside three distinct auditoriums, establishing a new cultural landmark along the waterfront.
articles.content: After nearly a decade in development, the Shanghai Grand Opera House officially opened on October 17, 2026, along the banks of the Huangpu River. Spanning 146,786 square meters, the facility houses three auditoriums with a combined capacity of 4,200 seats, alongside rehearsal, production, education, exhibition, and hospitality areas. The project originated from a 2016 international competition win and was developed alongside the East China Architectural Design & Research Institute, Theatre Projects, and Nagata Acoustics. The defining architectural feature is a sweeping white roof that rises from the landscape in a continuous spiral, inspired by traditional Chinese fans and river movements. This rooftop functions as a public observation deck and gathering space requiring no admission. Inside, the 2,000-seat Harmony Hall features a dark-red interior tailored for vocal acoustics. It is accompanied by the 1,200-seat Soar Theatre for classical performances and the 1,000-seat Open Stage, which offers flexible configurations for experimental productions. The inaugural performance season runs through February 20, 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Ibrahim Mahama Show Is Headed to Paris—But Its Core Is in Ghana - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Ghanaian Artist Ibrahim Mahama Opens Major Exhibition at Fondation Cartier in Paris
articles.excerpt: Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama is preparing to open his most ambitious exhibition at the Fondation Cartier in Paris. Titled "The Harvest Season," the project brings together community-based works, royal stools from the Asante Empire, and the reconstruction of the Aboso Glass Factory.
articles.content:
Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama is launching "The Harvest Season," a major exhibition taking over the entire building of the Fondation Cartier pour l’art contemporain in Paris. Described by the artist as his most ambitious project to date, the exhibition features a new iteration of "Parliament of Ghosts," an installation incorporating discarded train seats, school furniture, and worn-out jute sacks, alongside approximately 200 restored royal stools from the Asante Empire displayed outside glass cases for public engagement.

The exhibition also highlights a newly created project titled Things Fall Apart, centered on the reconstruction of the abandoned Aboso Glass Factory established in 1966 by Ghana's first president, Kwame Nkrumah. Following the Paris presentation, the factory components will return to Ghana for permanent installation. Mahama's broader artistic practice involves directing sales revenue toward founding educational and cultural institutions in Tamale, such as Red Clay Studio and the Savannah Centre for Contemporary Art. The Fondation Cartier exhibition additionally features contributions from numerous artists, architects, and collectives.

articles.originalTitle: Meet the collectors | Laurent Dumas - Art Basel
articles.title: Laurent Dumas Opens Le Large Contemporary Art Center in Greater Paris
articles.excerpt: Emerige real estate group CEO Laurent Dumas is opening Le Large, a new contemporary art center in Boulogne-Billancourt on the western edge of Greater Paris, featuring an inaugural exhibition exploring Île Seguin's history.
articles.content: Laurent Dumas, CEO of the real estate group Emerige, channels his passion for architecture and construction into a new cultural venue. On October 17 and 18, 2026, Emerige opens Le Large in Boulogne-Billancourt on the western edge of Greater Paris, establishing a contemporary art center dedicated to showcasing excellence with a focus on artists living and working in France. Dumas states that giving back and sharing are essential. For its inaugural exhibition, titled 'Moteur Imaginaire', Le Large centers on the history of Île Seguin. Long known as 'Île Renault', the island hosted the French car manufacturer for nearly a century until the factory closed in 1992. The industrial site also played a significant role in the May 1968 protests due to its unionized workforce. Wishing to present the carmaker's rarely exhibited art collection to a broader public, Dumas enlisted Italian curator Cecilia Alemani, artistic director of the 59th Venice Biennale, to shape the vision. Alemani brought together around 60 artists, including Neïl Beloufa, Bianca Bondi, Théo Mercier, Jean-Luc Moulène, and Laure Prouvost. The exhibition runs from October 17, 2026, to March 7, 2027. Additionally, Laurent Dumas will converse with artist Eva Jospin on Thursday, October 22, 2026, during the Art Basel Paris 2026 Conversations program.

articles.originalTitle: Tate Modern exhibition explores Pictorialism and the birth of soft-focus photography - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Tate Modern Exhibition Explores Pictorialism and the Birth of Soft-Focus Photography
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern's new exhibition challenges the movement’s reputation as outdated and narrowly Western. The show traces the international networks and influence of Pictorialism beyond the birth of Modernism.
articles.content: Charmaine Toh, the Tate’s senior curator of international art photography, notes that Light and Magic is likely the institution's first revisionist photography exhibition. Pictorialism, a salon-based movement, is traditionally associated with soft-focus, artful pictures from the 1920s and 1930s, confined mostly to Europe and North America. However, curator Toh emphasizes that practitioners continued making such work into the 1950s and 1960s globally. The exhibition features works by pioneers such as Alfred Stieglitz, Clarence Hudson White, and Henry Peach Robinson, alongside French photographer Robert Demachy and Chinese photographer Luo Bonian. Toh defines Pictorialism fundamentally as a desire for photography to be accepted as fine art on a par with painting or sculpture. She highlights that international clubs, including the Linked Ring, the Photo-Club de Paris, and the Vienna Camera Club, established crucial networks that enabled photographers to disseminate their work across borders. The exhibition remains open at Tate Modern until 21 February 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Frieze London 2026 - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Frieze London 2026 Highlights Global South Focus and Art World Developments
articles.excerpt: The Frieze London 2026 fair draws attention with an increased representation of artists and galleries from the Global South. Alongside the fair, developments include strikes at Goldsmiths, new art fairs, and sector-wide sustainability regulations.
articles.content: At the 2026 edition of Frieze London, the balance of the Frieze Masters section shifts towards the Global South, featuring more non-Western art alongside galleries from North Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia. During Frieze week, a staff strike at Goldsmiths art school reached 130 days, marking the longest in UK university history as students report receiving no marks or feedback. Meanwhile, the New London Invitational art fair took over 12 rooms at the Chancery Rosewood hotel in Mayfair, and the Latin American art fair Paraíso launched its inaugural edition. At Frieze London, Okiki Akinfe won the inaugural 30,000-pound emerging artist prize from the Dasha Shenkman Focus Fund. Additionally, the European Union Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation requires art galleries, museums, studios, and auction houses to report and improve the sustainability of their packing materials.

articles.originalTitle: Factory in Bangladesh that "redefines manufacturing architecture" wins RIBA International Prize - Dezeen
articles.title: Bangladesh Rug Factory Wins the 2026 RIBA International Prize
articles.excerpt: Designed by Nakshabid Architects, the Green Field Factory in Rangpur has won the 2026 RIBA International Prize for its workplace design that challenges traditional hierarchies, passive cooling strategies, and focus on employee wellbeing.
articles.content: Located in Rangpur, Bangladesh, and designed by Nakshabid Architects, the Green Field Factory has won the 2026 RIBA International Prize. Commissioned by Karupannya Rangpur Limited, the seven-storey rug manufacturing facility is the fifth recipient of the biennial award presented by the Royal Institute of British Architects for the world's best new building outside the UK. Drawing inspiration from traditional Bengali homes, the design incorporates natural ventilation, courtyards, verandas, gardens, and a monumental green facade to minimize mechanical systems. To challenge workplace hierarchies, the building features a single main entrance with two grand staircases shared equally by all workers and management. Shared facilities include a rooftop daycare center, medical practice, grocery shop, and prayer room to support employees and the surrounding community. The RIBA jury praised the project for redefining manufacturing architecture by prioritizing employee wellbeing and supporting its female workforce. The winner was announced during the Stirling Prize ceremony in London.

articles.originalTitle: Awakenings: Artists and Curator in Conversation - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Hosts a Two-Part Conversation on AI and Art
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum welcomes Aziza Kadyri and Eunjo Lee as part of the Awakenings programme, examining how digital systems and artificial intelligence shape art practices. The event takes place on 17 October 2026 at V&A South Kensington.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a conversation series as part of its Awakenings programme, exploring the integration of digital systems and artificial intelligence into art and design practices. The event will take place on 17 October 2026 at the Hochhauser Auditorium within V&A South Kensington. The programme brings together artists Aziza Kadyri and Eunjo Lee in conversation with Contemporary Programme Curator Carrie Chan, examining how both artists draw inspiration from the museum collection and the role of technology in their work. The first session at 14.00 features Eunjo Lee discussing her work When the Void Gazes Back, which explores how artificial intelligence and data reshape spiritual awakenings and non-human consciousness through digitally sculpted films and sculptures. The second session at 15.00 features Aziza Kadyri, who will discuss her new commission Sender Unknown, an installation that reimagines textile traditions in Uzbekistan at the intersection of artificial intelligence, art, and craft in response to the museum's historic suzani collection. Kadyri examines how technologies that risk erasing histories can instead function as preservation tools. The event is free and open to the public, with advance booking required.

articles.originalTitle: In Conversation with Liu Jiakun, Dong Gong, and Luo Yujie: Small-Scale Timber Buildings—Why Build Them and How? - ArchDaily
articles.title: Small-Scale Timber Buildings and Architectural Design Competition
articles.excerpt: The second GoodOne Future Timber Architecture Design Competition opens registration to explore timber applications in urban regeneration and public spaces, featuring insights from lead judges.
articles.content: As timber architecture expands beyond traditional residential and rural settings into urban regeneration, commercial spaces, and public activities, the need for evolving new architecture grows. The second GoodOne Future Timber Architecture Design Competition aims to explore these questions. Jointly initiated by Hefei Jiuwucang Architectural Assembly Technology, Z/S Studio, and Luxelakes A8 Design Center, this year's competition adopts the theme A Fantastical Journey Within. It invites architects, designers, and creative practitioners worldwide and across disciplines to participate. Registration remains open until October 23, 2026, at 12:00 noon. The competition's three lead judges—Liu Jiakun, founder of Jiakun Architects; Dong Gong, founder of Vector Architects and foreign member of the French Academy of Architecture; and Luo Yujie, founder of LUO studio—shared their perspectives. Drawing on their respective design experiences, they discussed bamboo and timber, small-scale architecture, public space, construction principles, and long-term building operations.

articles.originalTitle: "Designed to Be Red”, the First Survey of Native Graphic Arts - ARTnews.com
articles.title: First Comprehensive Survey of Native Graphic Arts Opens in New York
articles.excerpt: New York's Poster House is hosting "Designed to Be Red," a milestone survey spanning two centuries and more than 60 tribes. Curated by Brian Johnson, the exhibition explores the history of Native graphic arts across five distinct themes.
articles.content:
New York's Poster House is hosting "Designed to Be Red," a comprehensive survey dedicated to Native graphic arts. Running through next February, the exhibition spans two centuries and incorporates works from more than 60 tribes and nations. Organized by curator Brian Johnson, a citizen of the Monacan Indian Nation, the show is structured around five central themes: Indigenous Joy, Creative Sovereignty, Protest, It’s Complicated, and Extractive Marketing. The sections wrap around a single gallery space, allowing visitors to begin from either end.

Johnson developed the exhibition in part to address historical omissions and misrepresentations within the graphic arts record. Participating artists include Kent Monkman, Anna Tsouhlarakis, and Jeffrey Gibson. Alongside traditional posters, the exhibition incorporates three-dimensional objects, such as a ceramic wampum belt drawing on Haudenosaunee traditions and a Navajo dye chart displaying plants used on wool. The project examines the intersection of craft, visual art, and design while presenting historical protest objects and contemporary creations within a unified institutional context.

articles.originalTitle: French collector François Pinault plans permanent hang in Venice - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Collector François Pinault to Mount Permanent Exhibition at Palazzo Grassi in Venice
articles.excerpt: Collector François Pinault, owner of over 10,000 artworks, announced plans to mount his first permanent exhibition at Venice's Palazzo Grassi in March 2027, featuring 106 major works by 54 artists.
articles.content: At age 90, collector François Pinault announced plans to mount a first permanent exhibition from his collection of over 10,000 artworks, opening in March 2027 at Venice's Palazzo Grassi. In an interview with Le Monde, Pinault stated that the display will feature 106 major artworks by 54 artists. Typically hosting temporary shows since its founding in 2006, Palazzo Grassi will now present a permanent hang because previous exhibitions only offered the public fragmented stories. Pinault explained that a permanent display allows works from different periods to sit side by side and show enduring questions. He cautioned that the show does not freeze the collection or serve as a final word, noting that his team's view of art continues to evolve. Known for collecting ultra-contemporary works and drawing toward marginalized or non-Western artists, Pinault emphasized that he pays no attention to passport or gender. Bringing under-recognized scenes to light invites audiences to step off well-trodden paths of Western art, he added.

articles.originalTitle: Sam Taylor-Johnson: The Self and the Portrait (Livestream) - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Sam Taylor-Johnson to Discuss Artistic Practice in V&A Online Conversation
articles.excerpt: Internationally acclaimed artist and filmmaker Sam Taylor-Johnson will discuss her new monograph and portraiture approach in an online conversation with journalist Tim Blanks.
articles.content: Artist and filmmaker Sam Taylor-Johnson will join journalist Tim Blanks in an online conversation hosted by the Victoria and Albert Museum. Scheduled for 12 November 2026 from 19.00 to 20.00, the talk will focus on her new monograph and her distinctive approach to portraiture. Tickets cost £8.00, with general booking opening on 19 October subject to availability. Spanning photography, installation and film, Taylor-Johnson has continuously explored boundaries between the private and public self, and she will discuss the evolution of her artistic vision. The event will be hosted on Zoom, with link distribution scheduled for the morning of the talk, and a recording will be provided for those unable to attend live. V&A members enjoy various benefits, and purchases from the museum shop support ongoing institution activities.

articles.originalTitle: Geometry that Generates Energy: The Solar Facade of Breidablikk Gården, Norway - ArchDaily
articles.title: Office Building in Norway Features Solar Energy Generating Facade
articles.excerpt: Breidablikk Gården in Haugesund, Norway, combines rooftop photovoltaics with an integrated solar facade developed alongside SolarLab, merging energy generation with the building envelope.
articles.content: Located in Haugesund, Norway, the Breidablikk Gården office building pairs rooftop photovoltaics with an integrated solar facade developed in collaboration with SolarLab. Designed by Asplan Viak, the east and west elevations feature angled panels oriented toward the south to boost energy yield while providing shading for the offices within. Addressing the region's low winter sun angles, the facade forms a repeated zigzag at each window, optimizing solar collection and reducing cooling requirements. The project achieves a peak photovoltaic capacity of 39.9 kWp, with the facade capable of generating approximately 100,000 kWh of electricity annually. Constructed using low-carbon wood and prefabricated wall modules, the building has attained BREEAM-NOR Excellent certification. Engineered for local rain and snow conditions, the ventilated rainscreen protects the primary structure while utilizing an iridescent surface treatment that interacts with changing daylight conditions in the urban setting.

articles.originalTitle: Carmody Groarke’s Addition to Design Museum Gent Reads as a Manifesto on Sustainable Design - Architectural Record
articles.title: Design Museum Gent's New Wing Reads as a Sustainable Design Manifesto
articles.excerpt: The Design Museum Gent in Belgium has been transformed into a space for public debate through a new extension designed by London-based Carmody Groarke and local practices, featuring a distinctive low-carbon brick made from local waste materials.
articles.content: Added to the existing museum complex in Ghent's historic center, the 23,680-square-foot new wing connects an 18th-century hotel, a 17th-century house, and a 1990s extension. The five-story building utilizes 82,000 Gent Waste Bricks developed with local consultant BC Materials, containing one-third of the embodied carbon of conventional bricks. Comprising crushed concrete, glass, and porcelain cured in hydraulic lime, the unfired blocks form the pale facades. The architects implemented solid wood framing, utilizing cross-laminated timber for walls, staircases, and elevator cores. The entrance gate was 3D-printed from recycled aluminum by Antwerp-based Unfold, while the lobby features wood blocks salvaged from a tobacco factory. The uppermost floor houses a free-to-access events space offering views of the urban environment.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026: performances, lectures, discussions, roundtables - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Biennale Arte 2026 Concludes at the Arsenale with a Public Program and Performances
articles.excerpt: The 61st International Art Exhibition, Biennale Arte 2026, concludes at the Arsenale from November 13 to 22 with a public program of performances, panels, and an assembly of artist collectives under Koyo Kouoh's curation 'In Minor Keys'.
articles.content: The 61st International Art Exhibition, Biennale Arte 2026, curated by Koyo Kouoh, concludes with a public program at the Arsenale in Venice from November 13 to 22. Spanning the final ten days of the exhibition 'In Minor Keys', the schedule features performances, lectures, debates, and roundtables, alongside an Assembly bringing together ten artist-led organizations and collectives. The program includes performances by artists such as Laurie Anderson, Ziad Antar, Tammy Nguyen, and Hagar Ophir. The gatherings provide spaces for artists, curators, and educators to share ideas regarding pedagogy, research, and community. Participating organizations include Denniston Hill, RAW Material Company, GAS Foundation, lugar a dudas, blaxTARLINES, Nairobi Contemporary Art Institute, Dar Jacir, Fresh Milk, Picha Collective, and Gudskul. The schedule also features lectures by guests such as Felwine Sarr and daily discussion assemblies.

articles.originalTitle: History of the Building - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: A Guide to the Building History and Archives of the National Gallery
articles.excerpt: The architectural evolution, extension projects, and archival resources documenting the National Gallery building in Trafalgar Square since 1838 are explored.
articles.content: Established in 1824, the National Gallery initially occupied John Julius Angerstein's former home on Pall Mall with 38 paintings. Following collection growth, Parliament agreed to construct a purpose-built home designed by William Wilkins, which opened at Trafalgar Square in 1838. Throughout the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, the structure underwent multiple alterations, including the addition of the Barry Rooms, the Northern Extension in 1975, and the Sainsbury Wing in 1991. The Sainsbury Wing reopened in 2025 following redevelopment, while a redeveloped Research Centre within the historic Wilkins Building is scheduled to open in 2028, followed by Project Domani developments. The Gallery Archive houses correspondence, board minutes, architectural drawings, and photographs documenting the building's history. Records prior to 1992 are also held at The National Archives. Public records remain accessible to researchers at the Research Centre by appointment.

articles.originalTitle: EXCLUSIVE: Dunhill Heads to Florence as Pitti Uomo’s Fall 2027 Guest Designer - WWD
articles.title: Dunhill Named Guest Designer for Pitti Uomo 111
articles.excerpt: Richemont-owned menswear house Dunhill will serve as the guest designer for the 111th edition of Pitti Immagine Uomo in Florence.
articles.content: Richemont-owned menswear brand Dunhill has been named the guest designer for the 111th edition of Pitti Immagine Uomo, with plans to present its fall 2027 collection on Jan. 14 in Florence. The fall edition of the trade event will run from Jan. 12 to 15. Organizers noted that the salon show will draw on the long-standing relationship between the English and the city of Florence. Dunhill creative director Simon Holloway stated that Pitti Uomo holds a singular place in menswear and expressed honor at the invitation to present the collection within the forum. Pitti Immagine executives highlighted that the brand's ability to draw on British sartorial tradition while reinterpreting it through a contemporary lens reaffirms the event's unique position on the international menswear calendar. Founded in London in 1893, Dunhill offers a full wardrobe of tailoring, outerwear, leather goods and casualwear under Richemont's luxury portfolio.

articles.originalTitle: The 90s: Art and Fashion - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Britain Explores the Art and Fashion Culture of the 1990s
articles.excerpt: Tate Britain is hosting The 90s: Art and Fashion exhibition, bringing together art, fashion, photography, and design drawing on curator Edward Enninful's experience.
articles.content: Tate Britain is presenting The 90s: Art and Fashion exhibition, examining a period defined by bold creativity and a rebellious spirit. Drawing on curator Edward Enninful's experience, the exhibition brings together photography, fashion, art, and design to explore a moment when a new generation transformed culture. The exhibition features works by artists and photographers such as Steve McQueen, Sarah Lucas, Yinka Shonibare, Corinne Day, and Juergen Teller, alongside designs by Vivienne Westwood, Alexander McQueen, and John Galliano. Visitors can experience the energy and cultural shifts of a decade that broke down boundaries between art, fashion, and popular culture. Key pieces in the selection include Mark Leckey's video work tracing British dance music culture, Yinka Shonibare's reimagining of colonial histories, and Steve McQueen's silent film Bear. The exhibition is on view from 8 October 2026 to 14 February 2027.

articles.originalTitle: In Oregon, an Elegant Mass-Timber Library by Holst Architecture Makes a Grand Civic Statement - Architectural Record
articles.title: Holst Architecture Completes Mass-Timber East County Library in Oregon
articles.excerpt: Designed by Holst Architecture and Adjaye Associates, the 95,000-square-foot East County Library in Gresham opens as a 163 million dollar mass-timber civic landmark.
articles.content: Located in Gresham, Oregon, the East County Library spans 95,000 square feet and represents a 163 million dollar civic investment designed by Holst Architecture in collaboration with Adjaye Associates. Built on a former transit park-and-ride parcel, the two-story structure stands 59 feet tall and features a board-formed concrete base supporting exposed heavy-timber columns. The design process involved extensive community outreach, leading to programmatic inclusions such as dedicated meeting spaces, recording studios, and an auditorium for local organizations. Working alongside mass-timber specialists Timberlab, the design team utilized 96 columns, 1,200 beams, and 300 cross-laminated timber panels left fully exposed without additional fire-resistant treatments. The interior accommodates open book stacks for 200,000 volumes, centered around a double-height atrium with a spiral staircase. Mechanical equipment and ductwork were strategically integrated into the basement and floor reveals to preserve the visual warmth of the timber structure. Overseen by Multnomah County Library representatives, the facility addresses demographic shifts and long-unmet regional needs in East Multnomah County by providing an open public platform for the surrounding communities.

articles.originalTitle: Boucheron Amps Up Its Spotlight in the U.S. with New Christie’s Exhibition - Robb Report
articles.title: Boucheron Expands U.S. Presence with Monographic Christie's Exhibition
articles.excerpt: French jewelry maison Boucheron aims to boost its recognition in the U.S. with a ten-day exhibition at Christie's headquarters in New York, showcasing its heritage from the 19th century to the present.
articles.content: Founded in 1858, French jewelry maison Boucheron launched a ten-day exhibition in collaboration with auction house Christie's following the opening of its North American flagship on Madison Avenue in New York two years ago. Entitled Boucheron: In Focus, a Monograph of a Visionary, the exhibition showcases the brand's craftsmanship legacy spanning nearly 170 years alongside its innovative spirit. CEO Hélène Poulit-Duquesne stated that the main purpose of the event is to communicate the brand's deep history. Housed within the midnight-dark rooms at Christie's New York headquarters, the selection features exceptional pieces ranging from 19th-century origins under founder Frédéric Boucheron to collections introduced earlier this year. The exhibition highlights historical archival items such as Lady Harcourt's 1924 diamond tiara and Mrs. Mackay's 1888 laurel wreath necklace. Additionally, the maison's recent high jewelry collections, Impermanence and Human Nature, are presented to the public. Utilizing unorthodox materials such as borosilicate glass, ceramic, and diamonds, these experimental collections attract clients focused primarily on contemporary creativity.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Announces 272 Exhibitors and Reconfigured Layout for 2026
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries for its 2026 edition, featuring a substantially reconfigured showfloor and a more focused gallery lineup.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories for its upcoming edition, reaffirming its position as a major commercial moment in the U.S. art market. Taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center from December 4 to 6, with VIP preview days on December 2 and 3, the fair introduces a substantially reconfigured layout based on feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee. The redesigned floor plan occupies approximately 12 percent less floor space, while the main Galleries sector features about 10 percent fewer exhibitors to create a more concentrated setting. The new layout organizes the space around four hospitality plazas instead of five, distributing blue-chip galleries throughout the showfloor to improve navigation and sightlines. The event spans multiple sectors including Galleries, Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey, welcoming more than thirty first-time participating galleries mostly through its project-based sectors. Zero 10 returns with an expanded presentation dedicated to digital art. Public outdoor projects, partner awards, and institutional collaborations will accompany the main exhibition throughout the week.

articles.originalTitle: Where 60 Years of Master Craftsmanship Meets Modern Luxury Tech - WWD
articles.title: Adrian Jules Combines HandTailored Craftsmanship With Modern Enterprise Technology
articles.excerpt: Established in 1964, Adrian Jules Custom Clothier has developed an enterprise resource planning system to streamline operations in luxury custom clothing.
articles.content: Founded in Rochester, New York, in 1964, Adrian Jules Custom Clothier integrates over 60 years of hand-tailored craftsmanship with enterprise technology. The company developed an internal Enterprise Resource Planning system to track garments from initial order entry through workshop cutting, construction, and accounting. The platform serves as a central hub for private-label tailors and retailers, offering real-time visibility into fabric availability, pricing, and high-resolution visuals from global vendors. Platinum division CEO Alex Roberti emphasized the company's commitment to family-run values and high quality, while operations president Arnie Roberti noted that technology has streamlined pattern introduction and inventory tracking. Additionally, Adrian Jules has expanded its offerings by creating pattern designs specifically adapted to women's body shapes, helping retail partners capture a broader luxury market.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Moldova Pavilion: HYBRIDREAMS – Imagining otherwise in times of crisis - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale Moldova Pavilion Hosts Roundtable on War and the Future
articles.excerpt: Marking Moldova's first official participation at the Venice Biennale, a roundtable discussion explores how war and current crises alter ways of imagining the future.
articles.content: Marking the Republic of Moldova's first official participation in the International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, the project On the Thousand and Second Night serves as the starting point for a roundtable discussion examining how war and contemporary crises reshape the future. Titled HYBRIDREAMS – Imagining otherwise in times of crisis, the event takes place on October 16 at the Chiesa dei Santi Geremia e Lucia in Venice, home to the Moldova Pavilion. Organized in collaboration with the European Cultural Foundation and the European Council on Foreign Relations, the program opens with a guided tour led by priest and architect Don Gianmatteo Caputo. Drawing from Pavel Brăila's artistic proposition of continuation, the discussion expands from Moldova's geopolitical realities to the broader future of Europe and political imagination in response to conflict. Moderated by curator Adelina Luft, the panel features former Foreign Minister Nicu Popescu, European Cultural Foundation Director André Wilkens, and art historian Silvia Eiblmayr.

articles.originalTitle: ENR 2026 Top 100 Green Design Firms and Contractors: Green Building Market Deepens - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Green Building Market Deepens While Navigating Cost and Policy Challenges
articles.excerpt: While sustainable design and contracting revenues are on the rise, industry stakeholders are grappling with challenges such as federal incentive rollbacks, rising costs, and data gaps.
articles.content: Last year, the revenue of the top 100 green design firms increased by 17.1% to $11.8 billion, while international green design revenue rose 18.3% to $2.15 billion. The revenue of the top 100 green contractors also increased by 5.9% to $101.9 billion. While growth varied across markets, the largest increases were observed in industrial processes, hotels, and health care. However, industry experts point out that the rollback of federal sustainability incentives has created a ripple effect on project costs. Jill Kurtz from Stantec notes that many projects face uncertainties regarding real-world performance, emphasizing that decisions should be grounded in building science and operational data rather than certifications alone. Renée Azerbegi of Mead & Hunt states that shifting policy priorities and reduced incentive programs have generated funding uncertainty. Anica Landreneau from HOK reported that clients are increasingly concerned about grid reliability and energy resilience. Contractors suggest that bringing designers and trade partners together early on is critical in translating sustainability goals into practical decisions.

articles.originalTitle: Cosima von Bonin’s soft toys storm the Petit Palais - Art Basel
articles.title: Cosima von Bonin Unveils Dollys & Beaux Exhibition at Petit Palais
articles.excerpt: German artist Cosima von Bonin presents the Dollys & Beaux exhibition at the Petit Palais for Art Basel Paris's public program, bringing together her fabric sculptures and soft toy figures.
articles.content: Kenyan-born German artist Cosima von Bonin is presenting the Dollys & Beaux exhibition at the Petit Palais as part of Art Basel Paris's public program. The exhibition features large-scale soft-stuffed leather, velvet, and mohair sculptures created by the artist. These figures, which previously appeared in Loewe's Fall/Winter 2026 collection show, establish a dialogue between contemporary art and fashion. The presented works include velvet St. Bernard dog sculptures with plush barrels around their necks, sea scallops, a hermit crab, an octopus, and a killer whale. Spanning a career of over 40 years, von Bonin's installations encourage open-ended interpretations from viewers rather than imposing a single narrative. Miu Miu serves as the official partner for the public program. Dollys & Beaux is on view at the Petit Palais from October 23 to 25, 2026, while Art Basel Paris takes place at the Grand Palais from October 23 to 25, 2026.
